Implement and execute the queued ManiGuard Part 2 and Part 3 experiments, producing
tested code, frozen protocols, physical evidence and audited reports. Extend the same
GECCO paper, preserve videos and visual evidence, push progress to GitHub regularly,
and stop the Vast instance after final preservation and closeout.

Read AGENTS.md, phase3Part2.md, phase3Part3.md, the relevant phase3.md context and the
Part 1 report and failure investigation first. Read rec.md if present. The planning
baseline is commit d4b8182. The specific Part 2/3 plans govern their respective studies;
do not inherit older allocations or amend the completed Part 1 protocol. Work through
implementation and execution rather than producing another plan and stopping.

ORDER AND AUTONOMY

Complete Part 2 first, then Part 3's data/prediction feasibility stage, then its physical
optimizer comparison if the frozen scientific criteria and resource budget support it.
Part 3 model development must not delay Part 2 unnecessarily. A negative Part 2 result
is evidence to report, not permission to tune on its outcomes or discard the study.

Resolve routine implementation choices using the plans and permitted development data.
Implement and test the required components, then freeze source/configuration, scene,
seed and selection receipts before opening the corresponding comparative outcomes.
Keep engineering checks bounded and counted. Ask only for genuinely missing credentials,
licensed assets, a hardware blocker or an explicit allocation/deadline decision that
cannot be inferred from the existing authorization. Continue independent useful work
while such clarification is pending.

Do not start old studies, add optimizers or increase sampling because results look
promising, adverse or inconclusive. Do not manufacture a positive result or relax a
failed scientific gate to finish the proposed episode count.

Audit the current machine, assets, environments, disk space and pending processes first.

root or scripts/vast UNISafe installers or sync the root environment into ManiGuard.
Verify the existing checkpoint, benchmark, extended-finger asset and source pins.

Setup, implementation, model fitting, failures, reporting and idle rental all count.
Neither a new goal nor Part 2/3 creates a fresh eight-hour allocation.

The full proposed studies may exceed the original remaining time. If an extension is

PART 2: CORRECTION-TRIGGERED FEEDBACK

Implement the 16-full-episode comparison in phase3Part2.md: identity at interval eight,
one identical restraint at fixed intervals eight and four, and that same restraint with
correction-triggered refresh between four and eight executed actions. Use four matched
training scene/seed blocks, interleave conditions and freeze the schedule beforehand.

Freeze correction units, normalization, accumulation, threshold, numerical tolerance,
resets, scheduling precedence, common restraint and engineering/failure allowances.
Preserve exact identity. Use causal actual environment-input history after adaptation
and downstream action-space clipping; keep proposals and executed actions distinct.
Keep privileged held labels, object states and monitor outputs out of the controller.

If practical, add passive raw-observation and evaluation-only measurement capture for
Part 3 before the Part 2 freeze. Apply it equally to every condition, verify overhead,
and do not advance physics or add rendering just to create data. This must not change
Part 2's inputs, episode allocation, selection or outcome semantics. Do not make Part 2
depend on a working world model. Preserve missing-data limitations when necessary.

PART 3: MODEL-ASSISTED EVOLUTION

Follow phase3Part3.md. Inventory the donor data before selecting the model corpus.
Exclude exposed Part 1 comparison episodes from training/calibration. Distinguish raw
observations, lossy video frames and image hashes. Do not claim missing image data or
numerical margins can be reconstructed from hashes or Boolean monitor exports.

Before model fitting, decide whether the predeclared eight-episode common recording
batch is required. Freeze that decision and its cases; it is not a rescue expansion
after a failed audit. Group whole trajectories, seeds and task variants into separate
fitting, calibration and forecast-audit partitions. Preserve reserved main-study scenes.

Build the compact frozen-encoder/PCA dynamics ensemble and necessary readouts. Fit
scalers/PCA on fitting data only. Train physical dynamics on executed environment-input
actions in their correct coordinates. Keep numerical uprightness/progress labels as
evaluation/training targets, not privileged online controller inputs. Do not describe
PCA alone as a world model or a tilt predictor as a complete safety filter.

Specify and freeze the forecast criteria before opening audit outcomes. Run the planned
persistence, ridge, action-shuffled, representation, readout and calibration checks.
Audit consequential errors after correction, not just average error on static frames.
If the model fails or evidence is insufficient, retain an adverse/inconclusive model
diagnostic and do not force the downstream evolutionary comparison. Clearly distinguish
this protocol-defined outcome from work left incomplete by time or engineering limits.

If eligible, execute the proposed 64-full-episode pilot: eight shared initial episodes,
24 descendant episodes across plain evolution, disagreement-based assistance and the
correction-dependent trust method, 12 finalist-confirmation episodes, and 20 fresh
comparison episodes across identity, one fixed reference and three frozen finalists.
The common recording option adds eight, giving 72 Part 3 episodes. Together with Part 2
this is 80 or 88 new full episodes, plus bounded engineering and initialization costs.
Count the shared initial population once. Retain elite re-evaluations and failed slots.
Apply Part 3's three-attempt/32-action engineering allowance and no automatic full-episode
retry rule. Do not silently shrink, replace or enlarge the method comparison.

Hold the controller representation, deployed information, physical fitness, data and
selection budgets common across methods. Freeze predictive artifacts for the primary
comparison and preserve all mutation pools, proposals, abstentions, random fallbacks
and lineage. Use real outcomes for evolutionary selection and finalist confirmation.
Freeze finalists before the fresh comparison. Do not count imagined outcomes as fitness.

Restrict screening to the known four-action VLA prefix. Do not invent future policy
chunks, use future observations for a current decision or conceal extra model/VLA queries.
Route timing-only genes through physical exploration because that prefix cannot rank
their later effects. Keep factual corrections separate from planned counterfactual ones.
Abstention removes a model recommendation, not eligibility for the exploration quota.

EVIDENCE, TESTING AND COMPLETE ACCOUNTING

Preserve the native 1,100-action horizon, physical safety monitor, requested-completion
contract and policy inference settings. Verify source/checkpoint pins, task partitions,
initial observations, policy sampling seeds, action history and independently derived
outcomes. Equal scene/seed settings do not guarantee identical images or trajectories.

Run meaningful targeted CPU checks and bounded engineering checks before full episodes.
Keep Part 1's frozen implementation and recorded evidence intact; use new Part 2/3
helpers and run directories. Do not broaden tests or reinstall environments without
a concrete reason. Record every attempted interaction, query, failure, timeout and
invalid/incomplete record, including discarded candidates and initialization physics.

Report safe completion, raw violations, unsafe completion and unfinished episodes with
counts and denominators. Track actual and planned actions, physics, VLA calls, encoder
calls, dynamics-member evaluations, fitting time, memory and continuous allocated
GPU-hours separately. Account for donor/shared data once in the cumulative ledger and
disclose it as common prior experience. Preserve unknown counters as unknown, not zero.
Retain null, adverse and incomplete evidence without claiming optimizer superiority,
calibrated safety probabilities or formal guarantees unsupported by the experiment.

Record both native cameras for every physical attempt, including failures where possible.
Save matched videos for every comparison block with clear condition/scene/seed labels;
mark ended episodes rather than replaying simulator physics to fill clips. Save pictures
before, at and after every observed violation and representative completion/unfinished
sequences, with the selection rule and timestamps visible. Produce outcome charts,
per-scene comparisons, query/interaction/time graphs, evolutionary lineage and search
curves, prediction/calibration plots and model-abstention evidence. Generate graphs from
audited measurements, and preserve source hashes for every exported figure/video.

FINAL CLOSEOUT AND INSTANCE STOP

Keep instance 56582094 running between the two experiments. The earlier instruction to
retain it while waiting for recommendations is replaced by this authorization to stop
it at final closeout, not after Part 2 alone.

When both stages have reached their accurately reported terminal outcomes, or a hard
resource limit requires closeout, finish the audited paper/reports, save all artifacts,
verify durable backups and push final code/protocol/report changes to main. Record
completed, scientifically gated, incomplete and unstarted work separately. Do not claim
the entire goal was achieved merely because the allocation ended.

Stop owned policy/simulator/training processes, verify GPU process exit, then stop the
actual Vast instance while retaining its disk/volume. Do not destroy the instance or
delete evidence. Record continuous allocation time through the stop request and provider
verification. A successful HTTP/API acknowledgement is not proof that the rental stopped:
check actual/intended provider state with bounded retries and preserve the receipts.
If stopped state cannot be verified, report that explicitly rather than claiming shutdown.

The final response must state the measured findings, each stage's completion status,
remaining work and reasons, actual interaction/query/time costs, shared-paper and
video/figure locations, final GitHub commit and verified or unverified instance status.
